name: DEUCE-TO-SEVEN LOWBALL
description: Deuce-to-Seven Lowball (also called Kansas City Lowball or Billy Baxter Lowball) is a draw poker variant where the lowest hand wins. Aces are always high, straights and flushes count against the player, and the best possible hand is 7-5-4-3-2 (hence 'Deuce to Seven'). It is the exact opposite of standard high poker except for the A-2-3-4-5 rule.

content.text: Deuce-to-Seven Lowball (also called Kansas City Lowball or Billy Baxter Lowball) is a draw poker variant where the lowest hand wins. Aces are always high, straights and flushes count against the player, and the best possible hand is 7-5-4-3-2 (hence 'Deuce to Seven'). It is the exact opposite of standard high poker except for the A-2-3-4-5 rule.

Country/Region of Origin: USA
Time Period: Mid-20th century
Historical Development: Named 'Kansas City Lowball' and 'Billy Baxter Lowball' after the player who won multiple world championships in this game
Cultural Significance: Popular in professional poker circles and card rooms

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 4-6
Partnerships: None - individual play

Type: Standard 52-card deck
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included (normally played without joker)
Card ranking: Standard for determining low hands

Standard 52-card deck
Poker chips for betting
Dealer button for blind games

Each player receives 5 cards face down
Dealing passes clockwise after each hand
Typically played with blinds (small blind and big blind)

items.text: Deuce to Seven Triple Draw: Players have three opportunities to discard and draw. After deal, first betting round; first draw and second betting round; second draw and third betting round; third draw and fourth betting round; then showdown. In fixed limit, bet size normally doubles after the second draw. When the dealer runs out of cards, discards are shuffled to form a new deck for replacements.

Deuce to Seven Double Draw: Similar to Triple Draw but players have only two draw opportunities. Three betting rounds: after the deal, after the first draw, and after the second draw. Same deuce-to-seven hand ranking at showdown.
